Definition: from G4862 and G5463; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate:--rejoice in (with).
BiblicalUsage: When the shepherd finds his lost sheep he calls his friends and neighbours together and says, Rejoice with me, and the woman who finds her lost piece of silver does the same. Paul says the members of the body rejoice with the member that is honoured, and he tells the Philippians that if he is offered upon the sacrifice of their faith, he rejoices and rejoices with them all. Joy in Scripture is rarely solitary; it calls for company, and the finding of one lost thing is enough to start the feast.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that joy doubles when it is shared, and I hold that rejoicing with others over what God has found is one of the purest pleasures He gives. My position is simple: a church that cannot rejoice together has not yet learned what it was saved for.
